title: Torsion length of a relation quotient from maximal-rank minors
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $F$, and normalized valuation $v:F\to\mathbf Z\cup\{+\infty\}$ with $v(\pi)=1$ and $v(0)=+\infty$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $P$ be an $s\times N$ matrix over $A$ [def-weil-matrix], let $L\subseteq A^N$ be the submodule generated by its rows, and let $q$ be the dimension of their span in $F^N$. Set $M=A^N/L$ and $T=\{m\in M:am=0\text{ for some }0\ne a\in A\}$. Then $T$ has finite length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and
$$\operatorname{length}_A(T)=\min\{v(\det P_{S,T_0}):S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\},\ T_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\},\ |S|=|T_0|=q\}.$$
Here $P_{S,T_0}$ is the indicated square submatrix. If $q=0$, its empty determinant is $1$ and the minimum is $0$. The formula permits $s=0$, $N=0$, $q<N$, and zero minors.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Lemma 2 and proof, printed p.66 (PDF page 72), the finite free relation-module calculation underlying the Jacobian formula. Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: If $q=0$, each row of $P$ is zero in $F^N$, hence zero in $A^N$ because $A\hookrightarrow F$ is injective. Thus $L=0$ and $M=A^N$ has no nonzero torsion: $ax=0$ with $a\ne0$ forces every coordinate of $x$ to vanish since $A$ is a domain. Consequently $T=0$ has length zero. The sole minor of size zero is the empty determinant $1$, of valuation zero. This also handles $s=0$ or $N=0$. Henceforth assume $q>0$.

source.place: Tag 02LY (definition-length), Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), and the empty determinant convention accompanying Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dvr-matrix-smith-powers] to $P$ with $n=s$, $m=N$ and the chosen uniformizer. It gives invertible matrices $U,V$ over $A$ and $D=UPV$ with nonzero diagonal entries $\pi^{e_i}$ for $1\le i\le r$ and all other entries zero. Over $F$, multiplication on the left by $U$ leaves the row span unchanged, since both $U$ and $U^{-1}$ express the rows in terms of one another. Multiplication on the right by $V$ is an invertible linear map of $F^N$. The first $r$ rows of $D$ are nonzero scalar multiples of distinct standard basis vectors, so their span has dimension $r$. Therefore $r=q$; no identification of integral module rank with field rank is being assumed. Put $E=\sum_{i=1}^q e_i$.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr); the elementary-divisor step in BLR 3.3 Lemma 2, printed p.66, expanded using the existing rectangular Smith node.

proof.text:
The map $x\mapsto xV$ on row vectors sends $L$ to the row span of $PV$, which equals the row span of $UPV=D$ because $U$ is invertible. Its inverse is $x\mapsto xV^{-1}$. Thus it induces an isomorphism from $M$ to $A^N/\langle\pi^{e_i}b_i:1\le i\le q\rangle$, where $b_i$ are the standard coordinate vectors. Sending a vector to its first $q$ coordinates modulo $\pi^{e_i}$ and its remaining coordinates unchanged gives an isomorphism
$$M\cong C\oplus A^{N-q},\qquad C=\bigoplus_{i=1}^q A/(\pi^{e_i}).$$
Indeed this coordinate map is surjective and its kernel is exactly the displayed row span; its inverse sends coordinate representatives to their class, independently of those representatives. Every element of $C$ is killed by the nonzero scalar $\pi^E$, whereas $A^{N-q}$ has no nonzero torsion. Hence this isomorphism identifies $T$ with $C$. An isomorphism preserves length because images and inverse images give inverse inclusion-preserving bijections on submodule chains.

source.place: Tag 02LY (definition-length); explicit diagonal-coordinate quotient in the elementary-divisor calculation of BLR 3.3 Lemma 2, printed p.66.

proof.text: For $e\ge0$, submodules of $A/(\pi^e)$ correspond to ideals $J$ of $A$ containing $(\pi^e)$: take preimage under the quotient map, with inverse $J\mapsto J/(\pi^e)$. Since $A$ is a PID and $\pi^e\ne0$, such a $J$ has a nonzero generator $a$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], $a=u\pi^j$ with $u$ a unit and $j\ge0$. The containment $\pi^e\in(a)$ forces $j\le e$ by valuation; conversely each $0\le j\le e$ gives such an ideal. Moreover $(\pi^j)\subseteq(\pi^k)$ holds exactly when $j\ge k$, again by valuation. Thus the entire submodule lattice of $A/(\pi^e)$ is the chain of these $e+1$ ideals, and its longest strict chain has $e$ inclusions. By the definition of length, $\operatorname{length}_A(A/(\pi^e))=e$. For $e=0$ the quotient is zero and the chain has no strict inclusion.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion, and Tag 02LY (definition-length); explicit cyclic-length calculation.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] successively to
$$0\longrightarrow C_k\longrightarrow C_k\oplus A/(\pi^{e_{k+1}})\longrightarrow A/(\pi^{e_{k+1}})\longrightarrow0,$$
where $C_k=\bigoplus_{i=1}^k A/(\pi^{e_i})$, the first map is inclusion in the first factor and the second is projection. These maps are respectively injective and surjective, and the kernel of projection is exactly the first factor. Starting with $C_0=0$ of length zero, Step 4 and induction give $\operatorname{length}_A(C_k)=\sum_{i=1}^k e_i<\infty$. By Step 3, $T$ has finite length $E$.

source.place: Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive); length sum in BLR 3.3 Lemma 2, printed p.66.

proof.text:
For a finite matrix $B$ write $J_q(B)$ for its ideal of $q$-minors [def-trf-minor-ideal]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] twice to a $q$-minor of $UPV$, first through the $s$ intermediate row indices and then the $N$ column indices. For row set $S$ and column set $H$ this gives
$$\det(UPV)_{S,H}=\sum_{|I|=|J|=q}\det U_{S,I}\,\det P_{I,J}\,\det V_{J,H}.$$
All coefficients lie in $A$, so $J_q(D)\subseteq J_q(P)$. Applying the same two expansions to $P=U^{-1}DV^{-1}$ gives the reverse containment. Thus $J_q(P)=J_q(D)$. This is an explicit calculation for the given matrices, requiring no independence-of-presentation or Fitting-ideal theorem.

source.place: Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet); Tag 07Z7 (more-algebra.tex, lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), basis-change computation; BLR 3.3 Lemma 2, last paragraph.

proof.text: A $q$-minor of $D$ can be nonzero only if its row set and column set are both $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, since any row or column with index greater than $q$ is zero. For these two sets the Leibniz formula has just the identity-permutation term, giving $\prod_{i=1}^q\pi^{e_i}=\pi^E$. This product is nonzero in the domain $A$. Hence $J_q(D)=(\pi^E)$, and Step 6 yields $J_q(P)=(\pi^E)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet), determinant convention; BLR 3.3 Lemma 2, final diagonal-product calculation.

proof.text: There are finitely many $q$-minors of $P$, and at least one is nonzero since their ideal is $(\pi^E)\ne0$. Let $d$ be the minimum of their valuations, ignoring zero minors whose valuation is $+\infty$, and choose a minor $a$ attaining it. The unit-power factorization gives $a=u\pi^d$, and each other nonzero minor $b=w\pi^h$ has $h\ge d$ and is a multiple of $\pi^d$; zero minors are also multiples. Thus $J_q(P)=(\pi^d)$. Equality with $(\pi^E)$ gives $d=E$: each generator divides the other, so their valuations satisfy both inequalities. Together with Step 5 this is the required formula. Unit pivots ($e_i=0$), a free quotient summand ($q<N$), and zero minors were all retained.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), final assertion; BLR 3.3 Lemma 2, minimum-valuation conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem length_torsion_quotient_eq_min_valuation_minors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] {F : Type v} [Field F] [Algebra A F] [IsFractionRing A F] (π : A) (hπ : IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A = Ideal.span {π}) (vA : AddValuation F (WithTop ℤ)) (hvA : ∀ x : F, 0 ≤ vA x ↔ x ∈ Set.range (algebraMap A F)) (hvπ : vA (algebraMap A F π) = 1) (s N : ℕ) (P : Matrix (Fin s) (Fin N) A) (q : ℕ) (hq : q = Module.finrank F (Submodule.span F (Set.range (fun i : Fin s ↦ fun j : Fin N ↦ algebraMap A F (P i j))))) : ∃ ℓ : ℕ, Module.length A (Submodule.torsion A ((Fin N → A) ⧸ Submodule.span A (Set.range P))) = (ℓ : ℕ∞) ∧ IsLeast (Set.range (fun ST : {S : Finset (Fin s) // S.card = q} × {T : Finset (Fin N) // T.card = q} ↦ vA (algebraMap A F ((P.submatrix (ST.1.val.orderEmbOfFin ST.1.property) (ST.2.val.orderEmbOfFin ST.2.property)).det)))) (ℓ : WithTop ℤ)
